lines.text: Ausgerechnet hat das übrigens ein Rechenzentrum. Fenster hat's keine.
lines.note: The forecast as a fact the screen delivers: whatever tomorrow brings was worked out by a computer that has never looked outside, so it fits every sentence.

lines.text: Oben steht die höfliche Fassung. Die ehrliche wär kürzer.
lines.note: Points at the plain bold sentence on screen and implies the Grantler's real version is a one-word curse (or a curt 'Passt.' on a good day), so it reads under good and bad weather alike.

lines.text: Die Figur steht bei mir rund um die Uhr. Arbeitsrechtlich ist das grenzwertig.
lines.note: The drawn figure as an overworked employee, with German bureaucratic understatement as the punch; about the screen's own drawings, not the reader.

lines.text: Bei jedem Wetter trägt die Figur mein Logo. Reiner Zufall.
lines.note: True to the drawings (every sprite has the TRMNL logo on its clothes); the screen owns up to its own product placement with a dry 'pure coincidence'.

lines.text: Das Wetter hat sich noch nie krankgemeldet. Leider.
lines.note: Reacts to there being weather again tomorrow, as always: the weather as a colleague who never calls in sick, and the Grantler wishing it would for once.

lines.text: Freitag. Da könnt ich Hagel malen, und alle hätten trotzdem gute Laune.
lines.note: Reacts to the 'Morgen · Fr' tag: the Grantler resents that on a Friday nothing he draws can spoil anyone's mood, so it works under any weather.

lines.text: Punkt, Punkt, Komma, Strich. Mehr hab ich für dein Gesicht nicht gebraucht.
lines.note: The figure's face really is two dots, a nose mark and a line; every German speaker completes the nursery rhyme with 'fertig ist das Mondgesicht', so it is a looks jab (round, simple face) built on the drawing.

lines.text: Die Schrift ist nicht zu klein. Du wirst nur alt.
lines.note: Ties to the reader leaning in to read the small text on the screen this evening; an eyesight and age jab, short and confident.

lines.text: Über meine Witze lachst du nie. Über deine eigenen jedes Mal.
lines.note: Reacts to the reader reading this very line: the screen sulks about never getting a laugh and nails a specific cringe habit.

lines.text: Was du gerade anhast, mal ich lieber nicht. Das Shirt vom Junggesellenabschied, oder?
lines.note: The screen draws outfits but refuses to draw the reader's actual evening clothes, then guesses the one shirt everyone in Germany wears at home; a hedged wardrobe jab.

lines.text: So viel zum Wetter. Jetzt zur Soße an deinem Kinn.
lines.note: Closes the forecast like a meeting agenda and moves to the next item: a specific, slightly gross jab at the reader standing in front of the screen after dinner.

lines.text: Auf dem Bild bist du die Hauptfigur. Im echten Leben wird das nichts mehr.
lines.note: The single drawn figure makes the reader the lead of the picture; the turn says that's the only place they'll ever be one, a worth jab.
